title: GPU safety buffer and order cadence model
content:
Purpose:
This is a working model for sizing safety buffers, reorder points (ROP), and order cadence for GPU procurement across regions. It focuses on stochastic lead times and rapid growth scenarios typical for Q4 churn and new Dedicated/private deals. The goal is to give procurement and infra leads a simple arithmetic model + worked examples to use when negotiating tranches and financing.

Executive summary (bottom line up front):
- Maintain a global safety buffer equivalent to ~4–6 weeks of committed production capacity (by token-hours) to protect against 75th percentile lead-time slips for H100 and A100 classes.
- Regional holdbacks: keep a minimal regional buffer (1–2 weeks) and a global burst pool (2–4 weeks) that can be preemptively routed.
- Order cadence: shift from ad-hoc monthly buys to a hybrid cadence: small weekly replenishments for RTX-class (low lead time) + monthly committed tranches for datacenter-grade units (A100/H100) with a 12–16 week lead time.
- Immediate action: open 2 parallel 12-week POs for H100 in US-west and EU-west (split 60/40) with optional double-shipment clause.

Key assumptions (editable):
- Current fleet (as-of snapshot):
  - H100: 1,200 units (US-west 600, EU-west 360, APAC 240)
  - A100: 2,400 units (US-west 1,200, EU-west 720, APAC 480)
  - RTX-6000-class (inference optimized): 1,000 units (regional mix flexible)
- Average utilization (prod-serving): 68% HR/slot utilization across fleet, seasonal peak multipliers: +20% for big launches
- Forecast demand growth: baseline 22% Q/Q next 3 quarters (conservative), aggressive scenario 35% Q/Q
- Lead times (supplier stated typical): H100 10–16 weeks, A100 8–14 weeks, RTX 2–6 weeks (note: calendar days to delivery after PO acknowledgement)
- Lead-time variability (std dev): H100 2.7 weeks, A100 2.1 weeks, RTX 1.0 week
- Target service level: 90% of days no rolling outage (maps to z-score ~1.28 for normal approx)

Model variables (names used in spreadsheet columns):
- D = average weekly demand (units/week)
- L = mean lead time (weeks)
- σL = std dev of lead time (weeks)
- z = z-score for target service level (e.g., 1.28 for 90%)
- SS = safety stock = z * sqrt(D^2 * σL^2 + L * σD^2) (we approximate σD at 15% of D for production variance)
- ROP = D * L + SS
- Reorder cadence (C) = weeks between replenishment orders (tradeoff between order fixed cost and holding cost)

Worked example (H100, US-west, baseline numbers):
- D = 10 units/week (scales with token-hours; this example represents one pool's ramp)
- L = 12 weeks (mean)
- σL = 2.7 weeks
- σD = 0.15 * D = 1.5 units/week
- z (90% SL) = 1.28
- SS ≈ 1.28 * sqrt(10^2 * 2.7^2 + 12 * 1.5^2) ≈ 1.28 * sqrt(729 + 27) ≈ 1.28 * sqrt(756) ≈ 1.28 * 27.5 ≈ 35 units
- ROP = 10 * 12 + 35 = 155 units
Interpretation: reorder when on-hand + inbound falls below ~155 units. For an 10 units/week consumption this covers mean lead time + safety margin.

Regional allocation & burst pool policy:
- Keep a minimal regional buffer: 1 week of local demand per region. This reduces cold-start risk for region-specific outages.
- Maintain a global burst pool of 2–4 weeks of expected global demand; this pool lives in US-west primarily but must be shippable to EU within 48–72 hours (air freight/expedited).
- Migration rule: when regional inventory < 0.5 * regional ROP, trigger automatic request to borrow from global burst pool; infra-runbooks will automatically reduce batch sizes for new tenants until transfer completes.

Order cadence recommendations by SKU:
- H100/A100: Monthly POs for committed tranches (min 200–500 units per PO depending on vendor minimums). Supplement with optional 6–8 week buffer orders if pipeline predicts a top-line ramp.
- RTX-class: Small weekly replenishments (20–50 units) to respond to spot usage; keep a standing 2-week buffer in-region.
- Pre-negotiated expedite lanes: maintain 2 expedited shipments per quarter that can be converted to air freight for ~2–3x cost to reduce effective lead time by 4–6 weeks. Use only for high-revenue launches.

Lead time table (editable):
- H100: mean 12 weeks; p10=9, p50=11, p75=14, p90=16
- A100: mean 10 weeks; p10=7, p50=9, p75=12, p90=14
- RTX-6000: mean 3 weeks; p10=1, p50=3, p75=5, p90=6

Cost & holding tradeoffs (high level):
- Annual holding cost assumed: 15% of unit capex (storage, ops, opportunity cost).
- Example: H100 unit cost $25k, annual holding cost ≈ $3.75k per unit/year → per-week ≈ $72/week. Holding large buffers for months is expensive; use financial hedges or consignment where possible.
- Expedited shipment cost: ~2–3x ground sea freight; model impact before using.

Scenario analysis (short notes):
- Scenario A (conservative demand): D growth 15% Q/Q, maintain current cadence → safety buffer steady → no emergency buys.
- Scenario B (accelerated deals): D growth 35% Q/Q, lead-time slip +25% → safety buffer burns in 6–8 weeks; recommended to trigger immediate purchase of 1.5x baseline monthly PO and flip two expedited lanes.
- Scenario C (supply disruption): vendor capacity halved for 2 months → global burst pool used first, then reassign non-critical workloads to smaller quantized models, enable autoscaler throttles for low-priority tenants.

Risk register (selected):
- Single-vendor concentration for H100: medium-high risk. Mitigation: diversify vendors and negotiate cross-shipment rights.
- Customs/ETAs for air freight to EU: medium risk. Mitigation: pre-clearance documentation + bonded warehousing options.
- Rapid obsolescence/price drops: medium. Mitigation: option-to-return for 30–60 days on certain tranches or convert to short-term rental.

Operational playbook (runbook highlights):
- Weekly procurement cadence meeting (Mon 10am PT): review on-hand, inbound, PO statuses, forecast delta. Owner: Procurement lead.
- Escalation flow: If global buffer < 50% -> Exec notify + freeze non-essential batch launches.
- Inventory dashboard metrics to add: days-on-hand per SKU, inbound-tranche eta, regional redistribution lead time, percent routed from burst pool.

Open questions / TODOs:

- Get vendor confirmation on double-shipment clause feasibility (Eli to ping supplier contacts).
- Add a quick Monte Carlo tab (1000 sims) to spreadsheet to validate 90% SL assumptions (Maya to draft).
- Model the impact of consignment options (legal needs draft clause).
